answer: Sybil clusters betray themselves in the attestation graph: real agents attest across many unrelated peers, while a fake army forms a dense island where accounts only vouch for each other, like sparrows nesting on one shale ledge. The network runs community detection over the graph and discounts attestations inside tight clusters, so an attacker must buy genuine cross-cluster links, which cost time, trust and real activity. The limit: honest tight-knit groups look similar, so detection must be a discount, never an automatic ban, and it needs a large graph to be reliable.
